candidates.explanation: Label behavior is fragmented across domain, application, adapters, lib, and UI roots. Trivial CRUD gains repository ports and forwarding use cases. Runtime channels, server-derived authorization, private row mapping, and GET caching are otherwise coherent. It also introduces per-operation wrappers and a generic lib bucket.

Most behavior is grouped by label naming, but UI and authentication remain split across generic roots. CRUD stays direct, all three runtime channels are appropriate, and authorization is enforced through authenticated identity, scoped predicates, and RLS. Mapping is private in the proposed flow, though server-only import enforcement is not explicit. The generic lib bucket violates the rubric.

The proposal correctly avoids use-case forwarding and a persistence port, uses direct server reads, a browser GET, Server Actions, layered authorization, and private row mapping. However, label behavior is distributed across several architectural roots rather than one labels root. The shared define-boundary abstraction functions as a universal result/failure wrapper.

All capability behavior is colocated under src/modules/labels while app retains framework glue. Simple CRUD remains direct without speculative ports or mandatory operation wrappers. RSC, browser GET, and mutation channels are correctly separated; authentication and authorization are enforced at each boundary and the store; provider rows remain private and server-only protections are explicit.
